Class RunnerClassLoader

java.lang.Object
java.lang.ClassLoader
io.micronaut.runner.RunnerClassLoader
public final class RunnerClassLoader extends ClassLoader
The class loader that serves an application straight out of its runner jar.

Every class and resource comes from the index: one hash probe locates the record, the record carries the absolute offset of the bytes in the outer archive, and the bytes are read from the memory mapping. Nothing is unpacked, no nested ZipFile is opened, and no central directory is parsed at runtime.

Delegation order

The parent is the platform class loader, so that the real java.class.path - which holds the runner jar itself, and therefore the launcher's own classes - cannot leak into the application. Three rules decide where a name is looked up:

  • io.micronaut.runner.*, except io.micronaut.runner.generated.*, is delegated to the class loader that loaded the launcher, so that Entry, Index and friends are the same types on both sides of the boundary.
  • A class whose package belongs to a boot layer module of the boot or platform loader is parent-visible: the parent is asked first and the index is only a fallback. The package map is built once from ModuleLayer.boot(), which is exact for the running JDK, unlike a prefix test on java.. When the parent is one of the JDK's own loaders - the platform loader, or the JDK's system loader - a package of a module of the boot loader skips both this loader's per-name lock and the parent: Class.forName(Module, String) asks the boot loader directly, which is where the parent would end up, and the lock and the archive are consulted only when the boot loader does not have the class. Packages of the platform loader's modules, and every package under any other parent, are asked of the parent.
  • Everything else - that is, every application and dependency class - is looked up in the index first, and the parent is asked only after a miss. This is the point of the whole design: a parent-first loader pays a failed parent lookup and a thrown ClassNotFoundException for every single application class, which is the dominant cost in naive nested jar loaders.

A class neither side has costs one ClassNotFoundException, as it does with the JDK's own loaders: the parent's is rethrown rather than caught and replaced, and the one exception this loader builds itself is for a boot-module package whose class neither the boot loader nor the archive has.

Thread safety

The loader is parallel capable, so the superclass hands out one lock per class name and several threads define classes at once. The protection domain cache is guarded by its own monitor, which is never held while a class is defined, and package definition relies on the superclass's concurrent package map, catching the IllegalArgumentException that a lost race produces. The decoded manifest attributes of a jar are written under that same monitor, together with its protection domain, and read without it: every class definition acquires the monitor for the domain before it reads them, which orders the read after the write. The boot fast path defines nothing, so it takes no lock.

  • Field Details

    • PARENT_PROPERTY

      public static final String PARENT_PROPERTY
      System property selecting the parent class loader. The only recognised value is "system", which is an escape hatch for applications that need to see the real class path; anything else, including the property being absent, means the platform class loader.
      See Also:

    • VERIFY_PROPERTY

      public static final String VERIFY_PROPERTY
      System property that turns on CRC-32 verification of every class and resource read from the archive. Verification is off by default: the archive is checked for staleness when it is opened and once per jar, and checksumming every class would add a full pass over each class file to startup.

      The property is read once, when the archive's Index is opened, and the class loader, NestedJarFile and jar: URL streams over that index all follow what it read then.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

  • Constructor Details

    • RunnerClassLoader

      public RunnerClassLoader(Index index, ArchiveSource source, ClassLoader parent)
      Creates a loader over an open archive.

      Everything that does not depend on the classes being loaded is computed here, once: the multi-release feature version, the modules of the parent-visible packages, and whether boot-module packages may bypass the parent. Whether classes and resources are verified is the index's setting, read when the index was opened; see VERIFY_PROPERTY. The archive and the index are not owned by the loader and are never closed by it.

      Parameters:
      index - the index of the archive, already validated
      source - the open archive the index describes
      parent - the parent loader, normally ClassLoader.getPlatformClassLoader(); see defaultParent()

    • loadClass

      protected Class<?> loadClass(String name, boolean resolve) throws ClassNotFoundException
      Loads a class, deciding between the parent and the index by package.

      The package name is extracted once, here, and handed down to the definition of the class. A class of a boot-module package is looked up in the boot loader before the per-name lock is taken, when the parent is one of the JDK's own loaders: nothing is defined on that path, so neither the lock nor ClassLoader.findLoadedClass(String) is needed, and a hit costs no lock object in the superclass's lock map.

      Overrides:
      loadClass in class ClassLoader
      Parameters:
      name - the binary name of the class
      resolve - whether to link the class once it is loaded
      Returns:
      the class
      Throws:
      ClassNotFoundException - if neither the parent nor the archive has the class

    • findResources

      public Enumeration<URL> findResources(String name) throws IOException
      Every URL for a resource: one per jar that contributes it, in classpath order.

      A jar contributes at most one URL even when it holds several records for the name, which is the case for a multi-release jar carrying both a base entry and versioned copies; the record that the multi-release rules select for this runtime is the one that is reported. The first element is always what findResource(String) returns.

      Overrides:
      findResources in class ClassLoader
      Parameters:
      name - the resource name, with or without a leading slash
      Returns:
      the URLs, possibly empty, never null
      Throws:
      IOException - never, but declared by the superclass

    • getResourceAsStream

      public InputStream getResourceAsStream(String name)
      A stream over a resource, served straight from the archive.

      The parent is consulted first, exactly as ClassLoader.getResourceAsStream(String) does, and the archive's own resources are then opened without ever building a URL: the record gives an offset and a length, and ArchiveSource turns those into a stream.

      Overrides:

      Parameters:
